title: Latency Sentinel: region ranking using p50/p95 and network-stability composite
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a stable region-ranking service ("Latency Sentinel") that ingests per-region latency quantiles (p50/p95) plus lightweight network-health signals (packet loss, tcp_retransmit_rate, control-plane errors) and produces a single sortable score used by the smart router. The score will drive primary region selection, tier routing (hosted/dedicated preference), and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when regions degrade.

Scope and constraints:
- Input telemetry sources: regional edge latency histogram (p50 & p95), edge -> egress network loss %, and recent request error-rate (5m window). No dependency on long-tail logs to avoid high-cost pipelines.
- Scoring window: 1m EWMA for p50, 5m EWMA for p95 with decay factor to dampen spikes.
- Output: numeric stability_score (0-100) and categorical health {OK, Degraded, Unhealthy}. Router uses stability_score primarily; category enables policing rules (circuit-breaker thresholds).
- Weighting policy (first iteration): stability_score = 100 - clamp( w1 * normalized_p50 + w2 * normalized_p95 + w3 * loss_ppm + w4 * err_rate, 0, 100 ). Default weights: w1=0.25, w2=0.5, w3=0.15, w4=0.1. We bias toward p95 to favor tail protection.
- Fallback mapping: each primary model variant has an ordered list of compatible variants (same tokenizer + tolerable quantization delta). When region score crosses Unhealthy, router attempts next variant in the list in same or alternate region per policy.

Telemetry processing design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use local edge aggregators to precompute quantiles to avoid central bottleneck. This increases eventual consistency but reduces cost and latency.
- EWMA on quantiles chosen over raw percentile recomputation to reduce memory and compute at scale. Risk: EWMA can under-react to sustained regressions; mitigation: add a fast-path spike detector for p95 jumps > 40% relative.
- Packet-loss is measured as fraction of failed TLS handshake / retransmit probes from edge -> cloud egress; this is a noisy signal so it is scaled down in the weighting.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement scoring library and local aggregator in runtime repo. Add unit tests and a synthetic telemetry harness. (dev branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123)
2) Shadow release: route 0% production traffic but compute scores and compare to existing region-decider traces. Monitor divergences on Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/region-routing/latency-sentinel
3) Canary: enable in 5% of routes with auto-fallback disabled to observe behavior.
4) Gradual ramp to 40% with auto-fallback on and metrics gating (SLA-based).

Metrics to track (dashboards and alerts):
- distribution of stability_score by region (p50/p95)
- count of fallback events per hour and per route
- false-positive fallbacks (where fallback increased latency/cost)
- routing churn (route reassignments per minute) – limit to reduce flapping
- cost delta when switching to different tiers/variants

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we incorporate cross-region load (egress bandwidth saturation) into the score? Proposed follow-up ticket to quantify signal value.
- Confirm legal/enterprise preference for region affinity overrides (some customers require strict region pinning). Policy hooks will be needed in Console.

Artifacts and references:
- Initial spec doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-fake-latency-sentinel-spec
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
- Validation dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/region-routing/latency-sentinel
- Related Linear: ENG-55000 (region telemetry pipeline v2)
